subject: Renewal structure: stair-step term + staged capacity upsell — operational playbook
messages:
From: Alex Moran <alex.moran@agilemetrics.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 18 May 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal and capacity bump — questions on term structure

Hi Priya,

We're starting to scope next year's plan and want to align on how we renew with Redwood. Our usage spiked in Q1 and we expect another 30-40% growth next 12 months. Two asks: 1) Can we co-term the three existing contracts (dev / staging / prod) into a single umbrella term? 2) Instead of a straight annual commit, can we do a multi-year staggered ramp that buys us discount protection but lets us step capacity each quarter?

Key constraints: procurement prefers a single annual invoice if possible (for forecasting), but engineering wants the ability to unlock burst capacity without renegotiation. Also, our legal team will push back on auto-renew unless there are clear opt-out windows.

Attached is our Q1 usage export so you can see the growth curve.

Thanks,
Alex Moran
Senior Cloud Architect
AgileMetrics

Attachment: AM-usage-report-Q1.xlsx (spreadsheet, 42KB)

From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Moran <alex.moran@agilemetrics.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 18 May 2028 12:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal and capacity bump — questions on term structure

Alex — thanks for the context and the usage export, that's helpful. High level response below and a practical proposal attached. I'll summarize then propose next steps.

Summary answers:
- Co-terming: yes, we can consolidate the three contracts into a single umbrella commitment with sub-allocations for dev/staging/prod. That simplifies procurement and reporting.
- Stair-step multi-year: we typically offer a ramp schedule with quarterly unlocks — customers get committed and optional burst bands. Discounts increase with committed volume and longer term.
- Auto-renew: we can include an auto-renew clause with a 60-day opt-out window for the customer and an annual review for pricing adjustments tied to usage bands.

Attached is a proposal (Redwood_StairStep_Proposal_v1.pdf) that includes: a 24-month base term, year 1 = baseline commit + two staggered quarterly unlocks, year 2 = larger committed floor, and an explicit burst pool that can be used at overage rates or pre-purchased. I included two pricing scenarios (conservative growth / aggressive growth) so procurement has options.

Next steps I suggest:
1) Quick sync (30m) with your procurement and finance to confirm invoice cadence (single annual invoice vs quarterly).
2) If procurement wants single invoice, we will align billing to an annual charge but include usage true-ups each quarter.
3) I'll loop in Kimberly (Sales Ops) and Jonas (Finance) on the operational amendment and the DocuSign flow.

Can you do a 30m call Monday morning PT?

Best,
Priya Natarajan
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Attachment: Redwood_StairStep_Proposal_v1.pdf (proposal, 85KB)

Thanks for the context. Short answers from Finance: we prefer either (A) annual prepay (simpler for forecasting) with an escrow-style adjustment for year 1 material downsizes, or (B) quarterly invoicing with an annual true-up. Both are acceptable; procurement's preference for a single annual invoice makes option A sticky but workable.

For the amendment:
- We'll use the co-terming template and attach a schedule with quarterly unlocked capacities (Q1: +10%, Q2: +15%, Q3: +5 optional burst at pre-negotiated rate).
- Auto-renew: 60-day opt-out window is OK. We'll call out price bands tied to committed tiers and a mechanism to decouple burst pool billing.

Next actions:

2) Priya to confirm the final commit numbers on the Monday call (Priya: please capture the chosen scenario: conservative vs aggressive).
